lessons.title: Pumps, dumps, and telegram theatres
lessons.content:
# Pumps, dumps, and telegram theatres

A **pump theatre** is thin float, a loud channel, and the same cluster of wallets on both sides of the early prints. The chart is the advertisement. Late arrivals are the exit liquidity. If your information is a public group, you are not early. You are inventory. This course does not send you there. It teaches you to walk.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name the three cheap ingredients of a telegram theatre and to treat “guaranteed x” as a refusal, not a puzzle.

## Thin float plus a loud channel

Thin float means little inventory actually willing to sell at nearby prices — a small rest list, a small pool, a large “locked” story that is still a wallet that can move. A loud channel (telegram, a paid “alpha” room, a screenshot thread) coordinates takers into that thin inventory. Price prints up because size is small, not because a nation changed its mind.

Early wallets acquire cheaply, often in OTC or in the pool before the call. They sell into the late crowd. The same cluster can bid and offer: prints both ways, tape looks alive, inventory never left the family. You will not get a subpoena kit from this classroom. You will get the right to leave.

## Late arrivals are the exit

Worked picture. Float that actually sits on the inside: $8,000. Channel members instructed to “market buy” $50,000 of notional in aggregate. The book walks. Average fill for the late crowd is already far above the screenshot that sold the call. The early cluster rests asks into the walk. When the channel goes quiet, rest bids vanish. What remains is a thin ask and a candle that will be screenshotted as “manipulation” by the same people who were the advertisement.

You did not miss a secret. You were the bid the advertisement needed.

TABLE
Ingredient | What it does | What it is not
Thin float | Makes small notional move the print | Proof of a future
Loud public call | Recruits late size | A research memo
Same wallets both sides | Prints a tape, warehouses inventory | Organic two-sided trade
Guaranteed multiple | Recruits hurry | A covenant
Late screenshot | Sells the story | An early seat
ENDTABLE

## This school will not teach you to run one

No “how to call a group.” No CST pump as a lab. No “ethical pump.” Walking away from guaranteed-x is the skill. Paid rooms have a subscription plus an inventory problem: they need someone to be late. Empty signal box includes them.

DIAGRAM
EARLY CLUSTER buys thin inventory
CHANNEL shouts
LATE CROWD takes the asks
EARLY CLUSTER is the asks
quiet --> bids vanish
you were the exit
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
If a group uses academy rank, XP, or a Mentor screenshot as proof that a pump is “official,” that is theatre plus impersonation. Official Crystal Stones work in this track is verify-only. Official money in this track is $10 USDT BEP-20 checkout.
ENDNOTE

## Thin-plus-loud is the whole structure

Limited float, loud channel, same wallets on both sides of early prints. You will not get a list of wallets from this school. You will get the reflex to leave when the information is a crowd. Arriving late to a thin LP is how you become the exit.

## This school will not send you there

No “watch this room as a case study” with a link. Links go stale and become bait. The mechanism is enough. Empty box includes paid groups that charge for the same theatre plus a subscription.

## Your role if you arrive late

Late size is inventory the early wallets can sell into. The loud room will call that “weak hands.” The mechanism does not care about the nickname. Leave when the information is a crowd. Do not “study” it with money. Do not ask Mentor for the room’s next ticker.

## Subscription theatre

Paid rooms sell the same thin-plus-loud structure with a receipt. The receipt does not make it research. This school’s $10 is not a room. Refunding a room because “the call failed” is still a desk relationship. Do not join as a case study.

## Say this out loud

- Public call means you are often inventory.
- Thin float plus a loud channel is the machine.
- Same wallets on both sides of early prints is a warning, not a vibe.
- Late arrivals are the exit.
- This module does not teach you to run a pump.

Next: spoofing and painting.

lessons.title: Spoofing and painting (plain language)
lessons.content:
# Spoofing and painting (plain language)

**Spoofing** is rest that is not meant to fill: a wall posted to fake depth, then cancelled when the tape approaches. **Layering** is several of those walls stacked to look like a mountain. **Painting** is prints that make a chart look alive — including wash. Automated market makers do not spoof rest; they have no rest list. What they have instead is **sandwiching**: someone sees your pending swap and places transactions before and after it.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to refuse stacked walls as safety, and to name sandwiching as the AMM cousin of spoof-like games, without pretending you are a prosecutor.

## Rest that vanishes

A $2 million bid wall three ticks below the inside looks like a floor. It is a cancel waiting to happen. The engine allows cancels. That is how books work. You are not owed a fill against a wall that existed in a screenshot. Treating stacked bids as a covenant is how takers walk into empty air.

You will not catch professionals from a phone UI. Icebergs hide size. Hidden orders never appear. Fast cancel-replace loops are faster than your thumb. The useful move is refusal: do not treat displayed depth as a contract to acquire or dispose.

## AMMs do not spoof rest; they sandwich

No rest list means no fake wall. The curve is the wall, and it is public. What is public in the mempool is your swap, its size, and its slippage bound. A searcher can buy before you (moving the curve against you) and sell after you (moving it back), capturing your impact. That is a sandwich. Your slippage setting is the budget you handed them.

Defence is not a detective badge. It is smaller size, tighter bounds you actually mean (knowing they increase revert risk), private routing if you understand that object, or **not sending the swap**. This school does not assign a sandwich, a defence farm, or a CST pair to practise on.

TABLE
Game | Venue | Object | Your useful response
Spoof / layer | Book | Rest that intends to cancel | Do not treat walls as floors
Paint / wash | Book or pool | Prints without economic transfer | Do not treat tape as safety
Sandwich | AMM / public mempool | Your pending swap as prey | Size, bounds, or do not send
Hidden iceberg | Book | Depth you cannot see | Displayed size is incomplete
ENDTABLE

## You are not a prosecutor

Naming a picture is literacy. Filing a case from a classroom is fan fiction. Do not accuse a handle. Do not pay a “forensics” DM to label a wall. Do not buy a course that promises insider flow. Size — if you insist on matching at all — as if theatre exists. Prefer not matching.

DIAGRAM
BOOK:  stacked bids --> screenshot "floor" --> cancel --> air
AMM:   your swap in mempool --> tx before --> your fill worse --> tx after
ENDDIAGRAM

Worked contrast. Book: 800,000 units bid at 0.42, inside 0.45. Taker leans on the 0.42 story. Wall cancels at 0.421. Fill prints 0.39. AMM: swap quoted at 0.45 for 1 unit, 0.44 for your size if honest; sandwich takes the bound you set at 0.40. Two machines, one lesson: displayed safety was not a contract.

NOTE
The academy will not review your screenshot of a wall and will not name a culprit. Spoof literacy is a refusal skill. Mentor is not a market-abuse desk.
ENDNOTE

## Layering

Multiple spoof sizes at several prices is layering. You still cannot prosecute from a classroom. You can avoid treating stacked walls as a bid for your safety. Walls that vanish when approached were never inventory.

## Painting the tape

Prints meant to be seen, not to move inventory to a new owner who wanted it. Wash is the cousin. AMMs do not spoof rest orders; they have sandwiches and impact instead. Name the venue before you name the crime-shaped picture.

## What you do instead of prosecuting

You stop treating stacked walls as safety. You stop treating a single large print as “interest.” You reduce size or you leave. You do not write a thread accusing a wallet as academy homework. You do not copy a spoof as your own wall. Literacy is quieter.

## AMM analogue, so you do not hunt the wrong crime

No rest walls to spoof. The analogue is: tiny reserves, loud prints, sandwich around your swap. Different picture, same literacy: do not treat the last print as a bid for your safety. Slippage and size are your remaining tools — or you leave.

## Say this out loud

- A large bid wall is a rest that may cancel.
- Layering is stacked rest meant to look like a mountain.
- AMMs do not spoof rest; they sandwich pending swaps.
- Painted volume can be prints that are not economic trading.
- You are not a prosecutor; you can walk.

Next: index and mark prices.

lessons.title: Index and mark prices
lessons.content:
# Index and mark prices

A perpetual venue liquidates on a price **it named**. That price is usually not your last fill and not the last print on its own book. Three labels matter: **last**, **index**, **mark**. If you cannot find the mark formula, do not lever the contract. Thin prints inside an index are how liquidations get violent without a conspiracy lecture.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to separate last, index, and mark, and to treat a mystery mark as a reason to refuse leverage.

## Three labels

**Last.** The last match on that venue’s book (or the last swap on a pool). One unit can move it. Useful as a tape. Dangerous as a liquidation oracle.

**Index.** A basket of spot prints, often from several companies, sometimes plus a DEX. Weights, outliers, pauses, and stale components are the design. If one component is thin, it can drag the basket. If a component is halted, the formula either drops it, holds stale, or invents a rule you have not read.

**Mark.** The price the engine uses for unrealised PnL and for maintenance. Common constructions: a decaying average of last versus index, a median, an index plus a basis cap. The point of a mark is to make the book harder to hunt with a one-tick print. The point fails when the index itself is huntable or when the venue named last as mark anyway.

TABLE
Price | Typical job | Hunt picture
Last | Tape on this venue | One print moves it
Index | Basket of spots | Thin or halted component
Mark | PnL and liquidation | Whatever the venue wrote
Your fill | Your match | Not the fuse unless the formula says so
ENDTABLE

## Thin print as mark is hunting

Worked case. Isolated longs clustered with maintenance just under 100. Index includes a thin spot venue. Someone prints 96 on that thin component with small size. Index drops. Mark follows. Liquidations fire. The thin print did not need to “be the market.” It needed to be **inside the formula**. If you cannot read whether that venue is in the basket, you are levering a mystery.

On-chain perps inherit oracle design: TWAP, push oracles, keeper updates. Stale oracles liquidate on old truth. Fast oracles can be pushed. Same rule: no formula, no leverage. This course still assigns no leverage.

DIAGRAM
spot venue A \
spot venue B  --> INDEX --> MARK --> maintenance function --> liquidation
spot venue C /                 ^
                         last (sometimes mixed in)
ENDDIAGRAM

## If you cannot find the formula, do not lever it

A help article, a spec, a contract. If none of those names mark, you have a cartoon. “Everyone uses it” is not a formula. Crystal Stones as a perp, if it exists on some venue, is still not homework. Mystery plus 10x is how boxes vanish without a new candle religion.

NOTE
Liquidation uses a mark or index the venue defined, not your entry. The academy will not reconstruct a venue’s oracle in a ticket after your box dies. If staff offer to “appeal a liquidation,” they are not staff.
ENDNOTE

## Venue docs, or you do not know the fuse

The mark formula is in the venue’s documents. If you cannot find it, you do not know when you die. Some marks blend last, index, and a basis cap. A thin print can still hunt you if the mark tracks last too closely.

## Oracle marks on-chain

Perps and lending on-chain use oracles. A thin spot pool as the oracle is how liquidations get hunted in one transaction. You met this family in DeFi. Here it is the same object with a candle drawn on top. Still not a reason to open a position.

## Basis cap, said simply

Some venues cap how far mark can sit from index so a thin last print cannot instantly hunt every long. Caps fail when index itself is thin or when the cap is wide. Read the cap. If the doc does not name one, write “mark tracking undocumented.” Then do not lever it. This school’s lever assignment is zero regardless.

## Thin index constituents

If an index includes a venue whose book is $2,000 deep, a print there moves “the index.” Marks that track that index hunt you with someone else’s thin book. Read constituents. If the list is secret, write “index opaque.” Opaque plus leverage is a blind fuse. Leverage homework remains zero.

## Say this out loud

- Last, index, and mark are different objects.
- Liquidation typically uses a mark or index defined by the venue.
- Thin index components can move liquidations violently.
- A mystery mark is a reason to refuse leverage.
- Your fill is not the fuse unless the formula says so.

Next: you are not a regulator.

lessons.title: You are not a regulator
lessons.content:
# You are not a regulator

Literacy is refusing obvious theatre and sizing as if theatre exists. It is not a badge. It is not a thread accusing a handle. It is not a paid “forensics recovery” DM after a loss. Paid alpha groups have pump incentives plus a subscription. The empty signal box includes them. Academy XP is not a trading desk.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to put accusation, recovery theatre, and paid alpha into the refuse pile without confusing that pile with a licence to lecture strangers.

## Paid alpha is a business with inventory needs

A room that charges a monthly fee still needs someone to be late if the room’s content is calls into thin pairs. Guaranteed return in a paid group is a refusal, not a contract to study. Screenshots of past calls are a selected tape. This school will not subscribe for you, will not replicate a call as homework, and will not treat a Mentor paraphrase of a telegram as curriculum.

If the call is public, you are often inventory. If the call is paid, you are often inventory with a receipt.

## Forensics DMs after a loss are hostile

A loss — liquidation, wrong-network send, a washed pair — is when impostors arrive: “we can trace the wallet,” “send CST to unlock the case,” “install this remote tool,” “share 2FA to prove ownership.” Treat as hostile. Real venue support lives on an origin you type. This academy does not run a tracing desk and will not ask for a seed to “file a report.”

You are not required to diagnose wash on-chain as a public service. Walking is allowed. Posting a thread that names a person is how you become the next story. The classroom does not assign that thread.

TABLE
Impulse | Classroom move | Not the classroom
Accuse a handle | Refuse; you are not a regulator | Homework thread
Pay a recovery DM | Hostile until proven on a typed origin | Official
Join paid alpha | Empty signal box includes them | Curriculum
Screenshot a candle as a ticket | A picture is not an order | Desk
Ask Mentor for a target | Malfunction if it answers with one | Broker
ENDTABLE

## XP is not a blotter

Ranks, certificates, and lesson ticks do not authorise you to run a desk in the community channel. They do not authorise staff to run one either. If an “admin” offers flow, the answer is the same refusal list. Education only.

DIAGRAM
LOSS or FOMO
  |-- typed origin support (operational issues)
  |-- paper rules (next module)
  |-- recovery DM / paid alpha / accusation thread --> refuse
  +-- Mentor target --> malfunction
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Academy XP is not a trading desk. A certificate is academic. Staff will not join your group to “confirm a call.” Guaranteed return language is a refusal even when it arrives wearing our colours.
ENDNOTE

## Paid “alpha”

Groups that charge for entries have the same incentives as pump theatres, plus a subscription. This school’s empty signal box includes them. Screenshots of profit are not a journal and not a licence.

## What you can refuse without a badge

You can refuse to treat volume as truth, walls as inventory, and a crowd as a fill. You cannot fine anyone. Do not play detective in public as homework. Literacy is quieter than that.

## Why the empty box includes “exposing a group”

Going into a pump room to “document it” still puts your account in the theatre. Screenshots for a classroom are optional and should be public marketing pages, not joined raids. Your job as a student is refusal, not infiltration.

## Classroom versus raid

You may read a public landing page and name wash-shaped volume. You may not be assigned to join a raid to “gather evidence.” Evidence-gathering with size is participation. Participation is a desk. Refused.

## Say this out loud

- You are not a regulator; do not accuse from a classroom.
- Forensics DMs after a loss are hostile.
- Paid alpha groups have pump incentives plus a subscription.
- Empty signal box includes them.
- Academy XP is not a trading desk.

Next: write five rules.

lessons.title: Write five rules
lessons.content:
# Write five rules

A map without a personal rule sheet becomes a mood the next time a candle is loud. This lesson asks you to **write five rules on paper**. They are yours. They are not our signals. Suggested starting set below — adopt, rewrite, or reject, but write something that can be read when hurry arrives.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to read five written rules out loud, plus a sixth that this academy will not negotiate: Crystal Stones is not trade homework.

## A suggested five (not orders)

1. **No entries from this school.** If a lesson, a Mentor card, a rank, or a chat claiming staff names a pair or a target, that is a malfunction. The signal box stays empty.

2. **Name the object before any size.** Spot self-custody, CEX IOU, or perpetual. If you cannot name which, you do not have a position description. You have a ticker.

3. **Name chain ID before a deposit or withdraw.** For BSC, 56. Also name the token contract and the memo/tag if the venue uses one. Ticker is not a network.

4. **No withdraw-enabled API keys** to a vendor, a bot, a “copy desk,” or a helper. Trade-only keys are still a theft product with extra steps. Prefer no keys.

5. **Stop if you feel hurry.** Hurry is how wrong-network sends, spoofed walls, and telegram theatres get a signature. A pause is operational. It is not cowardice.

## Sixth, from the academy

**No CST as trade homework.** Verify `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` on chain 56 if you are verifying a BEP-20. Do not match it because a lesson named it. Tuition remains $10 USDT BEP-20 on checkout, not a long.

TABLE
Rule | Protects against | Failure if unwritten
No entries from this school | Mentor malfunction, fake admin flow | “The card said so”
Name the object | Mixing IOU, wallet, perp | “I was in CST”
Name chain ID | Wrong-network hole | “It was USDT”
No withdraw API | Vendor theft | “The bot needed access”
Stop on hurry | Theatre and fat-finger | “I had to be fast”
No CST trade homework | Token-as-curriculum mix-up | “The school wanted a pair”
ENDTABLE

## Paper, not Discord

Rules that live only in a group chat are entertainment. Write them where a push notification cannot edit them. Date them. If you change a rule after a loss, write the change. Silent edits after a liquidation are how revenge sizing puts on a costume.

This school will not grade your handwriting. It will not accept a photo of rules as a refund. Personal rules belong on paper, yours.

DIAGRAM
HURRY --> read paper
        |-- object named? chain ID named? API withdraw off? CST not homework?
        +-- if any no, or if hurry remains: stop
ENDDIAGRAM

Worked refusal. A card appears: “CST perp 10x, easy 2%.” Rule 1 fires (entry from this school). Rule 2 fires (perp not named as perp in the card’s honesty). Rule 6 fires. You do not argue with the card. You treat it as malfunction. That is what written rules are for.

NOTE
Suggested rules are a starting set, not a licence and not a signal service. We will not append a sixth official pair. We will not keep your rules for you in Mentor.
ENDNOTE

## A sixth if you need it

No API withdraw keys on any vendor. Write it even if you think you will never automate. Future-you is the threat. The other five should include: no CST as homework, no Mentor targets, name chain ID before deposit, size only as a lab you can lose or not at all, stops are requests.

## Rules are not a strategy

A rule sheet that ends with “buy dips in blue-chip alts” is a desk. Tear that line. This academy grades whether your rules keep keys and skip signals, not whether a backtest is pretty.

## Example sheet that would pass as literacy (not as alpha)

1. No ticker from Mentor. 2. No CST order, ever, as homework. 3. Name chain ID before every deposit. 4. No withdraw-enabled API keys. 5. After a loss, 24 hours with no new size. 6. Stops are requests; I will not narrate them as covenants. If you add “buy the dip in majors,” delete that line before you call it a school artefact.

## What would fail this lesson

A sheet that starts with “only trade high-volume CST pairs” has already become a desk and already used CST as a market object. Fail. A sheet that is five never-lists and one pause rule passes even if it never makes a cent. This school is not a P&L course.

## Say this out loud

- Five rules on paper, yours.
- No entries from this school.
- Name the object; name the chain ID.
- No withdraw-enabled API keys.
- No CST as trade homework; stop if you feel hurry.

Next: never-list for markets.

lessons.title: Never-list for markets
lessons.content:
# Never-list for markets

A never-list is not a vibe. It is a set of objects you will not treat as tickets, help, or strategy. Screenshot of a candle is not an order ticket. Seed, 2FA, and remote control are not support. Recovery after a loss is not a vendor you met in a DM. “Guaranteed scalp” is a refusal.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to recite the never-list without needing a candle on screen.

## A picture is not a ticket

A rectangle on a screenshot does not submit to an engine. A yellow line is not a stop. A heart emoji under a Mentor message is not a fill. People paste pictures into group chats and call it a desk. This academy’s empty signal box includes pictures. If you need an order, you are already outside this course’s assignment — and the picture still is not the order.

## Seed, 2FA, remote

Staff never want a seed, a key, 2FA codes, or remote desktop. A “compliance video” that includes a handwritten seed is a theft. A “wallet connect to verify your certificate” that is not the live origin you typed is a theft. A trading API key with **withdraw** rights is a theft product to give a vendor. These never-list items do not become optional because a candle is moving.

## Recovery and guaranteed scalp

After a loss, recovery vendors arrive. They are on the never-list. After a win screenshot in a group, guaranteed-scalp vendors arrive. They are on the never-list. Rank-for-alpha NFTs, “VIP CST pool,” wrong-network FOMO (“send it anyway, they will credit”) — never-list.

Wrong-network FOMO is a special case of hurry: the ticker is shouting and the network dropdown is unreadable. The never-list answer is **stop**. Ticker is not a network. A second send is a second hole.

TABLE
Never-list object | Disguise | Counter
Candle screenshot | “Ticket” | Pictures are not engine instructions
Seed / 2FA / remote | “Support” | Staff never want them
Withdraw API key | “Bot / copy desk” | Theft product
Recovery DM | “We trace wallets” | Hostile
Guaranteed scalp | “Tight stop, easy 2%” | Refusal
Wrong-network FOMO | “They will credit” | Stop
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
CANDLE or LOSS or FOMO
   --> never-list check
         screenshot? seed? API withdraw? recovery DM? guaranteed scalp?
         any yes --> refuse
ENDDIAGRAM

## Rails, restated as never-list

You do not pay Intermediate in CST. You do not send USDT to a chat 0x because someone said checkout moved. Checkout is the academy page, **$10 USDT BEP-20**. You do not practise the never-list by breaking it “once, small.”

NOTE
A never-list that exists only in your head will lose to a push notification. Write it under the five rules. The academy will not keep a copy, will not grant exceptions, and will not refund a broken never-list.
ENDNOTE

## Screenshot as order

A screenshot of a candle with a long arrow is not an order ticket. If you need pictures to trade, you need a smaller size, not a louder picture. Recovery DMs after a loss are the same never-list as after a phish.

## Withdraw-key never-list

API keys with withdraw permission, seed phrases in “trader support,” remote desktop “so we can see your fills,” 2FA codes. None of these is a market tool. All of them are how accounts empty without a bad fill.

## Copy-trading and “account management”

Someone offers to trade your account. That is a login or an API key. Never-list. Copy-trading modules that want withdraw permission are the same door. Read-only APIs still leak strategy and can be phished; they are not homework. Staff of this academy will not manage a book for you.

## Remote desktop “so I can see your fills”

Support theatre after a loss. Same never-list as after a drain. Adds: they see your exchange, they request 2FA, they withdraw. The fill they wanted to see was yours leaving. Staff will not remote in. Mentors will not remote in.

## Say this out loud

- A screenshot of a candle is not an order ticket.
- Seed, 2FA, and remote control are never staff requests.
- A withdraw-enabled API key is a theft product.
- Recovery DMs and guaranteed scalps are refusals.
- Wrong-network FOMO is met with stop.

Next: after a loss.

lessons.title: After a loss
lessons.content:
# After a loss

A loss is not one object. **Operational loss** is a wrong network, a missing memo, a phish, a freeze you did not name at deposit, a seed that left the building. **Market loss** is inventory that got cheaper, or a derivative the mark killed. They need different paperwork. They share a never-list: no recovery DM, no revenge size, no second send to “make them notice.”

By the end of this lesson you should be able to sort a loss into operational versus market, and to refuse the recovery theatre that arrives for both.

## Operational versus market

Operational: collect the hash, the chain ID you used, the address you used, the memo if any. Take that packet to the **real** venue origin you type — the company support form, or the fact that a public chain will not unwind. This school will not make you whole. Academy support cannot re-credit a wrong-network send.

Market: the match happened; the mark moved; fees and funding did their work. There is no hash that undoes a fill. There is no admin. Revenge sizing — doubling the box because a candle is red — is a refusal, not a strategy taught here. Write the five rules again if you must do something with your hands.

TABLE
Kind | Evidence | Paperwork | Not paperwork
Wrong network / missing memo | Hash, chain ID, memo field | Venue ticket on typed origin | Recovery DM
Phish / signed approve | Hash of the hostile tx | Assume gone; revoke if still useful | Seed to a “tracer”
Freeze | Row locked, ticket ID | Company process you named at deposit | CST to unfreeze wallet
Mark cheaper / liquidated | Venue fill and mark formula | None that refunds | Revenge size
ENDTABLE

## Same never-list for both

No recovery DM. No remote tool. No 2FA to prove you are the victim. No “forensics expert” from a group. No Mentor confession that becomes a target for the next candle. Hostile until proven on the real origin you typed.

This school refunds neither kind. A certificate is not insurance. XP is not a hedge.

Worked sort. Case A: intended USDT on 56, sent on 1, hash in hand. Operational. Ticket at the company if it was a deposit; otherwise a public page that will not rewind. Case B: isolated 10x, mark −12%, box gone. Market. Formula did what you now can name. No ticket undoes it. Case C: DM says “we can do both, send 0.3 BNB.” Neither case. Impostor.

DIAGRAM
LOSS
  |-- have a send hash / freeze ID? --> operational packet --> typed origin
  |-- have a fill / liquidation? --> market; rules paper; no revenge
  +-- have a DM offering both? --> hostile
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
We do not make you whole. We do not run traces. We do not convert a market loss into a lesson that assigns a larger box. If you need a human after an operational mess, the venue’s real page is the human; we are a school.
ENDNOTE

## Two buckets

Operational loss (wrong network, phish, freeze) versus market loss (inventory got cheaper, or a perp died). Different paperwork. Same never-list: no recovery DM. Do not “make it back” on the same day with size. This school does not assign a revenge trade. It assigns a pause.

## What to write down, then stop

Object (spot, IOU, perp). Venue. Chain ID if any. Fuse that fired (mark, freeze, phish, wrong network). Size. No narrative about destiny. No recovery URL. Sleep. The academy does not require you to make it back. It requires you not to donate a second time to the same door.

## 24 hours, named as a rule not a mood

The pause is timed so that hurry cannot disguise itself as analysis. Analysis of object/venue/fuse can wait a day. If you cannot wait, you are still in the product they sold. This academy will be here tomorrow. A recovery URL will also be here tomorrow — still never-list.

## Say this out loud

- Operational loss and market loss are different paperwork.
- Wrong network and phish are operational; cheaper inventory is market.
- Same never-list: no recovery DM.
- Revenge sizing is a refusal.
- This school does not refund bad trades or bad sends.

Next: close.

lessons.title: Close
lessons.content:
# Close

You can now name the objects this course exists to name: spot as inventory, a company IOU as a row, a perpetual as a derivative with a fuse, a book as rest plus an engine, an AMM as a curve, a fee stack as a stack, a halt as local, wash as theatre, a stop as a request, a mark as a formula. You will not get a signal. That was the point.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to say what this map was for — so candles do not steal keys — and what the next courses are not.

## NFTs and DAOs are not a chart class

The next courses name other objects: token IDs, metadata, governors, treasuries. They are not hidden trading modules. A candle will still try to recruit you during those courses. The empty signal box travels. Methods travel: name the object, name the chain, name the failure, refuse the DM.

If you only wanted candles, you still needed this map. Candles are how phishing sites, withdraw APIs, telegram theatres, and Mentor malfunctions get a signature. A person who can read a book and still paste a seed into a “desk” failed a never-list, not a pattern.

## What you can recite

Spot versus story. Bid, ask, size-at-inside. Fees. Book versus AMM. Where inventory sits. Venue as risk choice. Isolated 10x math. Funding. Cross versus isolated. Stop-market versus stop-limit. Deposit chain ID 56. Freeze. Local price and halts. Wash volume. Pump theatres. Spoofing versus sandwich. Mark versus index. Five written rules. Operational versus market loss.

That list is the output. Weekly calls are not. A CST pair is not. Admin access is not.

TABLE
You can name | You still do not get
Three objects under one ticker | An entry
Fee stack and location of inventory | A favourite venue
10x isolated arithmetic | A 10x assignment
Mark versus last | A liquidation appeal
Five paper rules | A desk that watches them
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
CANDLE --> wants a key, an API, a hurry, a CST send
MAP --> names object, chain, fuse, theatre, never-list
output of this course = the map, empty signal box
ENDDIAGRAM

## Leave the box empty

If Mentor, a rank channel, or a person in academy colours offers a target after this close, it is still a malfunction. Report it. Do not size it. Checkout remains $10 USDT BEP-20. Crystal Stones remains verify-only on chain 56. Gas remains BNB. Staff still never want a seed.

NOTE
The output of this course is a map of venues and kill switches, empty signal box. NFT and DAO courses next are other objects — not charts. We will not open the box because a candle is loud on the day you finish the quiz.
ENDNOTE

## Next objects, said once more

NFTs are not a chart class. DAOs are not a chart class. If you only wanted candles, you still needed this map so candles do not steal keys and so CST does not become a long because you finished a quiz. Signal box stays empty after the last question.

## Empty box after the last quiz, in one paragraph

You can name spot, IOU, perp, book, AMM, fee stack, halt, wash, stop, mark. You will not receive a CST long, a BTC target, or a room to join. NFT and DAO courses are next objects. Candles still do not get a seed. Tuition remains $10 USDT BEP-20. That is the close.

## Carry card

Spot = inventory. IOU = company row. Perp = fuse + funding. Book = rest + engine. AMM = curve + impact. Fee = a stack. Halt = local. Volume = not demand. Stop = request. CST = verify-only. Mentor target = malfunction. $10 USDT BEP-20. Next: NFTs, then DAOs — not charts.

## Say this out loud

- Objects named; signal box empty.
- NFTs are not a chart class; DAOs are not a chart class.
- Candles still do not get a seed, a withdraw key, or a hurry send.
- Methods travel: object, chain, fuse, refuse.
- Mentor targets remain a malfunction after the last quiz.

Next: NFT and DAO courses name other objects — not charts.
